briefing:
### The window in one sentence

The week of September 19--25 showed a strong acceleration in the second half, with sessions nearly doubling from first half to second (76 to 143, +88%), driven by a burst of content modifications that landed Thursday through Friday. GSC data is absent for this window, which limits search performance visibility and needs immediate attention.

---

### Volume + composition

Over the 7-day window (September 19--25), the site logged 219 sessions, 192 users, and 720 pageviews, averaging 31.3 sessions and 27.4 users per day. Those averages are in a reasonable range for BCC's traffic level, though the daily spread was wide -- weekend and early-week days sat in the low-to-mid 20s while the back half of the week pushed into the 40s.

Channel composition this week inverted the expected baseline. Organic Search led at 100 sessions (46% of total), well above the expected ~25%, while Direct came in at 88 sessions (40%), below BCC's typical ~60% share. Email contributed 13 sessions, Referral 14, and Unassigned 15. That Organic Search surge relative to baseline is a positive signal -- it suggests either a ranking improvement or that some of the recently modified pages are drawing search-driven clicks that were not there before. The Unassigned bucket at 15 sessions is worth a look; those are likely tagged or linked visits that GA4 could not attribute cleanly, possibly from social posts or an untagged URL in a newsletter.

GSC impressions and clicks both show zero across every day of the window. This is almost certainly a data pipeline issue -- the 30-day efficacy rollup shows 1.47 million attributed impressions, so the site is clearly indexing and appearing in search. If GSC data is genuinely missing from the daily pull, that gap needs to be resolved before next week's briefing, because it makes it impossible to monitor click-through rates or validate which modified pages are generating search visibility.

---

### Trend (first half vs second half)

The halves split tells a clear story: the first three days of the window (September 19--21) generated 76 sessions and 192 pageviews. The final four days (September 22--25) generated 143 sessions and 528 pageviews -- an 88% session increase and a 175% pageview increase. That is a genuine acceleration, not noise.

The pageview-to-session ratio also shifted noticeably. In the first half, visitors averaged about 2.5 pageviews per session. In the second half, that climbed to roughly 3.7 -- suggesting that whoever came to the site later in the week was exploring more pages per visit. That lines up with the session duration anomalies flagged on September 23 (+136%) and September 24 (+381%), where average session length spiked well above the 28-day median. Fewer people came on September 24, but the ones who did spent significantly more time. Taken together, the back half of this window brought more engaged visitors, likely connected to the cluster of page modifications that went live September 23--25.

---

### Launches + efficacy

This was a high-output week with meaningful content shipping across both blog posts and service pages. The most significant launch in terms of raw GSC exposure is the hydration post -- "/healthy-living-2/why-hydration-is-essential-for-weight-loss-and-management/" -- updated September 24, which is already showing 344,397 total GSC impressions and 1,716 clicks (0.5% CTR) with 369 GA4 sessions attributed. That is the top-performing content asset in the current top-launches list by a wide margin, and it is only 3 days post-modification. The CTR at 0.5% is low relative to the impression volume, which suggests the title or meta description may not be doing enough work at the SERP level -- worth revisiting.

The page modifications on September 25 produced mixed early results. "/what-is-a-weight-loss-counselor/" is showing 1,082 impressions and 14 clicks (1.3% CTR) with 7 GA4 sessions in just 2 days -- a solid start with a CTR that beats the hydration post. "/nutritional-counseling-in-san-antonio-tx/" has 3,854 impressions but zero clicks, which is a flag: strong visibility, no action. That almost always means the title and snippet are not matching searcher intent well enough to earn the click. "/bariatric-therapy-in-san-antonio-tx/" has 8 impressions and no clicks -- too early to draw conclusions, but the low impression count suggests it may not yet be indexed or is targeting a very narrow query set. The "/start/" page shows 3 sessions and no GSC activity, which is expected for a conversion-focused page that does not target informational queries.

On September 23, a meaningful cluster of service and program pages also went live: "/emotional-eating-therapy-in-san-antonio-tx/", "/overeating-treatment-in-san-antonio-tx/", the Testimonials page, Dr. Sara Hamilton's bio page, and three program sub-pages (dietitians, community, cooking). None of these appear in the top-launches efficacy data yet, which likely means their impression counts are low or attribution is still accumulating. These pages are 4 days old as of this briefing -- too early to judge, but they should be watched closely next week. The gastroparesis post ("/diet-and-nutrition/gut-health/gastroparesis-aka-stomach-paralysis/") updated September 24 is showing 20,351 impressions and 49 clicks at a 0.2% CTR -- high visibility, weak click pull, similar pattern to the nutritional counseling page.

No new backlinks were earned in this window based on the ledger data. The existing backlink profile stands at 4 referring domains, 12 total inbound links, and 5 edu links. The edu link count is genuinely valuable and worth building on.

---

### What this means + what to do next

1. **Diagnose the GSC data gap first.** The zero-impressions-across-all-7-days pattern in the daily pull is almost certainly a pipeline or credentials issue, not a real traffic event. Resolving this is a prerequisite for accurate trend analysis going forward -- without it, the briefing cannot assess search momentum, rank movement, or whether content updates are driving SERP gains.

2. **Prioritize title and meta description rewrites for the two high-impression, zero-click pages.** "/nutritional-counseling-in-san-antonio-tx/" (3,854 impressions, 0 clicks) and the gastroparesis post (20,351 impressions, 0.2% CTR) are already visible in search but not earning clicks. Even a modest CTR improvement on the nutritional counseling page -- say, from 0% to 1% -- would mean 38+ additional clicks per data cycle. Rewriting the snippet to speak more directly to what a searcher at that query stage needs is the highest-leverage move on the board right now.

3. **Run a focused internal-linking pass on the September 23 service page cluster.** The emotional eating, overeating treatment, and bariatric therapy pages are new or freshly updated service pages with local intent. They will rank better and faster if they receive internal links from higher-traffic pages -- particularly the hydration post and the gastroparesis post, which are already drawing sessions. Connecting those content pages to the service pages creates a path from informational intent to conversion intent.

4. **Investigate the session duration spikes (September 23--24) to understand what content those visitors were reading.** Average session duration hit 246 seconds on September 23 and 502 seconds on September 24 -- both well above the 28-day median. High dwell time on a low-traffic day often means a small number of highly engaged visitors found something specific. Pulling the page-level detail for those two days in GA4 would clarify whether a particular page is resonating and worth expanding or promoting.

5. **Build a second edu backlink outreach effort based on the existing 5 edu links.** The site already has edu-domain links, which are among the most durable authority signals available. Identifying which institutions those links came from and finding adjacent departments, programs, or resource pages at those same schools -- or peer institutions in San Antonio -- is a longer play but one that compounds over time. One warm outreach per week is a sustainable pace.
